messages:
maya: Quick sync — I'm proposing an 8-week tile to shore up multi-tenant launch readiness. Main ask: align dependencies, owners, and showstoppers so we can publish launch criteria to sales by end of week 4.

maya: TL;DR goals:
- Deliver stable p95 latency < 200ms for tenant traffic at committed capacity
- Keep unit cost delta <= 15% vs baseline
- Provide a canary and rollback path for private tenant rollouts

maya: Primary technical dependencies I see:
- runtime: async prefetch + KV cache partitioning (so tenant cold starts don't spike latency)
- infra: tenant scheduling slots + prewarm/autoscale SLOs for burst protection
- security: KMS/HSM rotation acceptance & audit logging for private customers
- platform: canary harness + per-tenant tracing (for SLI calculation)

maya: Please reply with: 1) Are these accurate? 2) Who can own and commit to a week-3 checkpoint? 3) Any immediate blockers?

aj - eng: Accurate list from eng side. Adding: rollout gating in Console (route-level flags) and migration plan for existing tenant assignments.

aj - eng: I can own the Console gating work, aim for W3 demo. Need a runtime API for tenant pinning though.

vincent - runtime: Agree on prefetch + partitioning. Two notes: 1) prefetch prototype exists but needs hardening for eviction policy; 2) partitioning affects KV cache hit rate — we'll need perf benching on quantized models.

vincent - runtime: I can own the runtime API + prefetch hardening. Will need a 2-week spike (W1-2) and perf run in W3. Blocker: hardware for perf runs (need 2x A100 days).

maya: Noted — Vincent to own runtime spike. I'll coordinate hardware request with Tess.

tess - infra: Can allocate test capacity for perf runs, but prioritization ask: do we want dedicated nodes or burstable infra labs? Dedicated will give cleaner results but cost more.

maya: For the perf baseline we should use dedicated nodes for accuracy. For CI/integration we can use burstable.

tess - infra: Ok — I'll schedule 3 dedicated perf-days in W3. Also calling out autoscale policy changes: we need a gradual slot backfill (to avoid noisy neighbors). That requires a kube-scheduler tweak and a tuning window (2-3 days). Owner: infra (me) + runtime (Vincent) to validate.

sara - security: Two security items: 1) KMS rotation acceptance — need an integration test and audit log format; 2) private customer onboarding checklist (policy + encryption at rest) — that'll require a PA review.

sara - security: I can own KMS integration acceptance criteria. Timeline: integration test by W4. Blocker: access to customer KMS test keys (ask Liam to coordinate).

liam - cs: I can provide test keys for staging and draft the onboarding checklist. Also need a clear launch criteria doc to share with customers — can we produce that by W5?

maya: Yes — target is to have a short launch criteria doc (1 page) by W5 so sales/customer success can start comms. Liam to draft, Maya to review.

aj - eng: Minor but important — we must define rollback granularity: per-tenant toggle vs route-level fallback. Recommend route-level fallback as default, per-tenant toggle for customers with contractual SLAs.

vincent - runtime: Agree. We'll add a "fallback model" config and a tenant toggle. Implementation plan: API + KV flag store (W2), runtime check + fallback (W3).

tess - infra: One more infra risk: stateful KV partitioning requires migration. We need a migration runbook and a canary with 5% traffic. I'd like ops runbook authoring to be an explicit deliverable.

maya: Good call — deliverables list I propose:
- D1: Runtime spike + perf results (Vincent) — W3
- D2: Console gating and rollout UI (AJ) — W3 demo
- D3: Infra autoscale + scheduling changes + perf nodes (Tess) — W3 schedule + W4 validation
- D4: Security KMS integration test + audit format (Sara) — W4
- D5: Migration + ops runbook + 5% canary plan (Tess + Aj + Vincent) — W4
- D6: Launch criteria one-pager (Liam + Maya) — W5

maya: Immediate asks / blockers:
- Tess: confirm perf node dates and quota (Vincent needs hw)
- Sara: confirm access to staging KMS test keys (Liam to provide)
- AJ: estimate for Console gating (hours) so we can lock scope

aj - eng: Console gating estimate ~40–60h (including tests). Can compress if we scope to minimal UX.

tess - infra: Perf nodes booked: W3 day 3-5 (3 days). Quota request sent to cloud-ops.

sara - security: Liam — please DM me the provisioning flow for test KMS keys. I'll prep the integration spec once I have keys.

liam - cs: DM sent to Sara. Also adding a user story from a pilot customer: they require a documented rollback SLA. We'll need legal to sign off on what we promise.

maya: Noted, will loop in legal once we have a clear rollback doc.

cicd-bot: Deployed branch "tenant-qos/wip" to staging (sha: ab12c3) — smoke tests passed.

vincent - runtime: Nice. I'll queue a perf run against that branch on W3 nodes.

maya: Next steps / commitments:
- Vincent: runtime spike + perf W1–W3 (owner)
- Tess: infra perf nodes + autoscale tuning W2–W4 (owner)
- AJ: Console gating feature W2–W3 (owner)
- Sara: KMS integration spec & tests W3–W4 (owner)
- Liam + Maya: Launch criteria doc draft by W5

maya: I'll create a short RFC + tracker by EOD and tag owners. If anyone cannot meet these commitments, reply here with constraints.

aj - eng: If we can get the perf results by mid-W3, we can bake fallback tuning into the Console demo.

vincent - runtime: One constraint: we may hit a perf regression on a quantized variant. If that happens, we need a decision by W3 whether to accept cost delta or delay tenant rollout. I'll surface that early.

maya: Good flag — please call out regression severity levels in the perf report.

liam - cs: From pilot customer POV: they'd like an SLA for latency and an activation window. I'll capture exact asks and add to the launch criteria doc.

maya: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC link here when created. :thumbsup:
